key_insight: Unlabelled high-frequency probe data can be used semi-supervisedly to improve time-resolved flow reconstruction from sparse PIV snapshots, especially for physically consistent temporal gradients.
engineering_relevance: The method can reduce experimental burden while improving velocity and pressure estimation in aerodynamic flows where PIV is too slow to capture full dynamics.
method: Enrich sparse PIV training data by time-marching a simple advection model.
Train two neural networks: one for POD temporal coefficients and one for their time derivatives.
Use unlabelled probe samples plus least-squares regularization to enforce temporal consistency.
evidence_signal: Validated on synthetic turbulent channel flow and experimental airfoil wake PIV, where unlabelled probe data improved reconstruction accuracy and temporal smoothness, leading to better pressure estimates.
watch_item: Performance may depend on how well the advection model and probe coverage match the true flow physics; poor mismatch could weaken consistency enforcement.
paper_title: Data-efficient semi-supervised learning for flow estimation using unlabelled probe data
